newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude steady to up, ADNOC grades at discount.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude steady to up, ADNOC grades at discount.

text.p: Asia crude prices were steady to higher on Wednesday amid talk of ADNOC grades trading at a discount.
A Japanese trader was heard selling a cargo of Murban at ADNOC less six or seven cents and a cargo of Qatar Land at QGPC less three or four cents.
Traders remained wary of the deals until there was further clarification. The names of the buyers were not heard.
However, many players said they were expecting ADNOC grades and other MidEast grades to face downward pressure which could take them into discount territory.
Oman appeared to be firming with two majors said to have exchanged a cargo of April Oman at MPM +4.5 cents, up slightly from deals talked on Tuesday at MPM +3 cents and MPM +4 cents.
Elsewhere, two major Japanese players swapped a cargo of Murban and Qatar Marine.
Players in the regional market were gearing up for an expected weaker March market.

Official Indonesia export allocations were little changed from February, although players said they expected extra allocations to be made because of the 38-day turnaround of the Dumai refinery which is scheduled to start on Saturday.
That should push more Minas and Duri onto the market, so sentiment on price remained a 30/60 cents over ICP.
Bontang Mix was heard traded twice around a 10-cent premium, but little emerged on other grades.
A producer sold 650,000 barrels of March Tapis to a U.S. major at quotes +$1.10, which traders said was in line.
Various fields offshore western Australia were watching the weather with a tropical low threatening to build into a cyclone.
